titleStmt.title: Ovid, Amores 3.5: witness S — first-pass manuscript transcription
titleStmt.author: Publius Ovidius Naso

respStmt.resp: First-pass inspection of every extant verse image and manuscript encoding
respStmt.name: OpenAI Codex, encode_s agent

publicationStmt.p: Amores Project working transcription, 9 September 2026. Awaiting independent second source reading; not human scholarly approval.

handDesc.handNote: The main verse text is written in brown ink. Layout, visible signs and annotations are transcribed without assigning historical hands from colour alone. Long s and ordinary letter allographs are represented by standard Latin characters.

origin.p: The source manifest dates this composite manuscript to the 11th and 12th centuries. The catalogue date is not a date for every intervention.

surrogates.p: Actual source pages 390, 392 were inspected at full resolution and in enlarged crops. Viewer page numbers are one-based indices into the manifest, not manuscript page labels. e-codices IIIF source manifest

projectDesc.p: All 46 extant verse positions were first-read directly from witness S images. Existing annotation rectangles are reproduced without modification. No reading is supplied from LL or another witness. Word spacing and couplet grouping are editorial. Independent second reading remains required.

correction.p: Visible letters are retained even where they differ from familiar readings. Tentative paleography is localized with unclear. A missing written initial is represented as gap, without inventing its decoration. Marginal annotations are not silently substituted into the verse. Ink colour alone does not establish an erased reading or historical hand.

normalization.p: u/v and e caudata follow visible source forms as far as practicable. Long s and ordinary letter allographs use standard characters. Combining macrons represent visible suspension/contraction bars schematically. Abbreviations are paired with defensible expansions in choice/abbr/expan; unexplained letters are not expanded merely to match a familiar edition. Special glyph approximations are declared in charDecl. Their form is typographic rather than a facsimile drawing.

punctuation.p: Visible stops are transcribed as schematic dots or colons. Modern punctuation is not supplied. Word spaces are editorial except where space explicitly records a significant physical separation.

segmentation.p: Every verse has a stable ID and a facs pointer to a rectangle on the correct manifest canvas. Annotation page values are interpreted through the manifest index. Physical page changes are pb elements within logical couplets where necessary. Source text beyond the poem is used to verify boundaries but not included as verse.

interpretation.p: Notes are a first-reader evidence queue. Local uncertainty is documentation rather than an automatic user task. A different reader must independently inspect each verse and investigate all notes before integration.

div.head: First-pass encoding notes
div.note: A small n is isolated in the left margin, with broad uninscribed space before ox erat. It is retained as a manuscript guide-like inscription without inventing a completed large initial. The sōnꝰ contraction is faint and expanded tentatively; sūmisit retains its visible form. The right-margin inscription reads ad followed by abbreviated, faint words provisionally sōniū suū; these remain unexpanded. Both line-ending and marginal points are retained.
Nasal bars in animū and meū are preserved; expansion is encoded separately. A terminal point is visible.
The final us of creberrimus is a raised suspension; the source spelling and terminal point are retained.
The separate et sign and two terminal points are preserved schematically.
The full source line reads Area gramineo suberat uiridissima prato. Terminal points are retained; the source spelling is not borrowed from another witness.
The source begins humida and ends aquę. The final is of sonantis is crowded and touched by a high darker stroke; the local reading remains unclear. No erased letters or distinct hand are inferred.
Nasal contractions in uitabā and estū and the raised us sign in frondibꝰ are retained. The source has estum without an supplied initial a.

Arborea is visibly written in the main text. The sed abbreviation has a small ambiguous final stroke and remains qualified; tamē and estꝰ retain their source contractions. No normalized aestus is supplied.
The us suspension in floribus is encoded. The complete verse is visible in its selected rectangle.
The source has the barred forms tū cū, with no separate c after the first u. These are expanded as tum cum. Niuibus has a raised us ending, and terminal points remain.

Actual page392 begins with In liquidas, continuing the preceding verse on390. After mo there is a disturbed r-like baseline area and an a above; the tentative baseline and addition are retained without a conjectural deleted letter. The baseline of uertat is qualified at a, with a small i above it recorded as an annotation; cancellation is not securely established. The nondum contraction and terminal points are preserved.
The source clearly reads spumis. The quod sign is a crossed q with d; stridentibus ends in a raised suspension. No alternative from another witness is introduced.

The word after Et is an m with a small raised o, provisionally expanded modo. Siccatam and ouem are nasal contractions. Relinq(u)it appears in a compact barred form, represented schematically as reliq̄t; its expansion is kept separate from the written abbreviation.

The ending of felic̄ is partly stained and has a raised dark stroke. The abbreviation is retained unexpanded rather than silently asserting every letter of feliciter. Maritus has a raised us suspension.
Cumque, tenerum, coniuge, pressit and humum have visible contractions. The source has sua without a canceled following m; no other witness supplies a cancellation.
The opening is Dūq, expanded Dumque. There is no separate et sign between iacet and lente in this source line.
The source word is pasto, with a clearly visible p and long s. Atque and iterum are abbreviated. The point after cibo is retained.
The final form looks like ferentia rather than a simple final i. The a-like ending is retained as locally uncertain, not normalized. Somno and adimente preserve their visible nasal contractions.
The source word is deposuisse. Cornigerum, terra and caput are abbreviated; no normalized substitute is introduced.
Leuibus has a raised us sign. Pēnis has a nasal bar and is expanded pennis. The per sign before auras is a crossed p represented schematically.

The opening contraction is faint, provisionally Vēn and expanded Venit with low certainty. The source following garrula reads sedit. No exclamation mark or canceled ending from another witness is imported.
The visible source words are bouis niueę petulantia pectora. Their case forms and e caudata are retained without normalization. Terque is abbreviated.
Locum and taurumque have nasal contractions. The final reliq̄t is an abbreviated reliquit; its written suspension is not displayed as a fully spelled word.
The source explicitly has S̄ niger in uaccę pectore liuor erat. Sed is expanded separately, and the source word niger and e caudata are retained.
Utque, procul and uidit are abbreviated. The pro sign is represented schematically and receives an explicit expansion.
The source reads Carpebant tauri pabula lęta procul. The e caudata, pro suspension and terminal point are retained.
Gregibusque is abbreviated. The initial minim sequence of immiscuit is crowded; im remains locally uncertain while the rest is clear. The two terminal points are retained.
The source has herbę with a descending cauda and humum with a nasal bar. Fertilioris is visible here; no stain qualification from another witness is applied.

Nocturnę has e caudata. The following clustered abbreviation is provisionally qcūq, with a qualified expansion quicumque. Its exact first strokes need the independent reader; the source is not silently printed as a full modern word.
Both quid forms use qd contractions. The remainder of the verse is clearly legible.
The main source reads Sic ego nocturnę sic dixit imaginis augur, with ego rather than an inserted r. E caudata and terminal points remain.
Quem has a nasal bar and mobilibus a raised us sign. The complete line is present, through uolebas.
Sed is abbreviated; estus preserves the source spelling. The full line is legible.
Est is an e with a suspension bar and aptus has a raised us sign. Puellę retains its descending cauda; the terminal low point is represented schematically as a comma.
The source reads Tu uir and compare, with the ending e present. The separate et sign and terminal paired points remain.
Quod is a crossed-q abbreviation with d; the full line remains legible.
Ingenium and dominę have visible nasal or contraction bars. Lena is written without a definite descending cauda here. The line ends in anus and paired points.
The opening quod has a crossed-q abbreviation, taurum a nasal bar and reliquit a compact barred abbreviation. All are expanded separately.
The source reads in uacuo and thoro. Frigidus has a raised us suspension and the terminal point is visible.
The source has maculę and nigrę with e caudata and a separate et sign. No alternative case form is substituted.

Interpres is abbreviated. The small abbreviated form between gelido and sanguis has a high mark and is provisionally represented m̄, unexpanded until independently checked; it is not supplied from another witness.

The first word is contracted, provisionally Fuḡ with tentative expansion Fugit. Its point, the separate et sign and paired points after meos are preserved. Below the verse a small a and the indented mn(is) inscription start the next poem, establishing the boundary. No verse after46 is supplied.
